EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS

Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that are conventionally left off.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality add irrelevant personal information rather than evidence of fit.

items.says: The same onboarding result is attributed to both Harbor Payments and the hospital practicum, with conflicting reductions.
items.because: The practicum predates the internship and has a hospital client, making the result’s ownership and figures doubtful.

items.says: The 35% conversion increase has no stated baseline or measurement period.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale or meaning of the improvement.

items.says: The annual loss estimate lacks an annualization method and a definition of losses.
items.because: Six months of data do not by themselves establish the annual figure, and the line does not show how the interviews support it.

items.says: The measurement approach is given without the outcome it found.
items.because: The method alone does not show whether the redesign changed onboarding or what the comparison demonstrated.

items.says: The quantified time-to-first-payment result comes after the activity details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the outcome that shows the scale of the work.

items.says: The opt-in comparison alone does not establish that the redesign caused the reduction.
items.because: Merchants selected their own flow, so differences between the groups could explain the outcome.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the reported rate, not actual late deliveries.
items.because: Changing the population counted does not change whether those shipments were late.

items.says: The 30% reduction lacks a measurement basis.
items.because: Without comparable measurements, a reader cannot assess whether the figure supports the claimed result.

items.says: “Prepares” is in the wrong tense for a role that ended in 2023.
items.because: It breaks tense consistency with “Coordinated” and may make the role seem current.

items.says: The annual savings result comes after the rollout and training details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the outcome that shows the scale of the work.

items.says: The annual driver-hours savings figure lacks a measurement or estimation basis.
items.because: Rollout and training do not by themselves establish an annual total.

items.says: The launch bullet gives reach but not what made the pickup service operational.
items.because: A reader cannot see the product or operational skill behind the result.

items.says: The wording does not clarify the relationship between the students and dining halls.
items.because: A reader may misread the service’s scale or operating model.

items.says: The weekly sessions are described without saying what they changed.
items.because: “Working sessions” is vague and does not show the value of the contribution.

items.says: The passive phrasing hides the candidate’s actions, and the shortened form has no measure of its effect.
items.because: Adoption alone does not show whether intake became faster, simpler or more accurate.

items.says: The practicum bullet wrongly assigns a merchant-onboarding result to a hospital-network project.
items.because: It describes merchants and reproduces a result attributed to Harbor Payments.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding bullet does not fit the hospital-practicum narrative.
items.because: The other practicum bullets concern clinic operations, leaving the practicum’s work unclear.
